newsitem.title: PERU: Lima embassies beef up security in hostage crisis.
newsitem.headline: Lima embassies beef up security in hostage crisis.

text.p: Major embassies in Lima have beefed up security during the nearly month-long hostage crisis at the Japanese ambassador's residence, diplomats said on Monday.
But there have been no other reported threats to embassies since Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels stormed the Japanese residence, where they still hold 74 hostages.

"Right after the incident broke out, the Japanese government demanded that all embassies overseas strengthen security measures," said an official of the Japanese government's task force monitoring the crisis. He added that the Peruvian government had increased the number of police guards at Japan's embassy in Lima.

U.S. Embassy officials said the number of guards at their fortress-style compound had also been increased. "We have to be prudent. We had hostages from the embassy," embassy spokesman David Kurakami said. Seven U.S. diplomats were released in the early stages of the crisis.
The homes of senior diplomats were being guarded around the clock and their vehicles constantly checked, added another official from a European country, who asked not to be named.

Scores of diplomats were among the more than 500 captives initially seized by MRTA rebels when they stormed a cocktail party at the ambassador's residence on Dec. 17, but most have been released. The ambassadors of Bolivia and Japan and about 12 other Japanese diplomats are among the 74 hostages still held by the rebels.
